sentences.text: As per the prosecution story, on 12.03.2023, 30 years old prosecutrix moved an application in writing before police alleging that her husband has died in the year 2017 in bus accident.
She along with her two children is residing at Chhatarpur and also run a small grocery shop for earning livelihood.
Six months ago her cousin has eloped with someone.
She had gone to lodge FIR and that time she met with Sourabh Bhatnagar who had assured her to get her cousin traced.

It is alleged that on 11.03.2023, at around 08:20 pm, when she was running her shop and her younger child was sleeping, Sourabh Bhatnagar reached to her shop by a vehicle purchased a cigarette and asked her to give a glass of water.
When she bent down to take water from the container, he came from the behind caught hold her and raped her in the shop.
When she attempted to save her Sourabh bit upon her thigh.
She sustained injuries.
FIR was registered and after investigation charge-sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that prosecutrix is a habitual to complainant and she makes complaint only to extract money from the people.
It is further submitted that victim has already been examined before the trial court.
She has turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution case.
Therefore, it has been prayed that appellant/accused be released on bail.
O n the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for objector have opposed grant of bail.

Learned counsel for the objector has submitted that prosecutrix had tendered her evidence before the trial court under pressure as she was threatened to kill, therefore, it is prayed that appellant be not released on bail.
Prosecutrix is a major lady.
On a perusal of her evidence recorded before the trial court, it is revealed that she has turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution story.

Considering the prosecutrix deposition before the trial court and the fact that appellant has no criminal background and is a member of Child Welfare Committee, Chhatarpur but without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the appellant/accused is not warranted.
Consequently, appeal stands allowed.

It is directed that appellant-Sourabh Bhatnagar be released on bail on h is furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
